Items.Authors: Mala Mateen, Kyler R. Langworthy, William J. Gibson, Scott C. Newey, Tanya C. Tavenner, Jack D. Drummond, Ian M. Kingsolver, James A. Mathis, Bryan J. Oas, Michelle M. Graebner, Michael B. Flanagan, John L. Wynia, Odell R. Reynolds, Robert L. Johnson, Patrick R. Kelly
Items.Title: First light results from Castor AO
Items.Abstract: An adaptive optics (AO) system was developed for the 1.0-meter Castor, ground-based, optical telescope. The system is operated by the Starfire Optical Range in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The system saw first light on 29 Jun 2025 and achieved diffraction limited imaging in I- and J-band. The adaptive optics system is located at coudé focus, and it features a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor that can operate in two optical configurations: 10×10 and 6×6 subapertures. The 10×10 configuration allows the correction of a higher number of modes, relative to the 6×6 configuration, which is optimized for dim objects detection. Wavefront sensing is performed at visible wavelengths, while tilt-control and AO-corrected imagery is made in the near-infrared. This paper describes the first AO observations, and presents the photometric measurements for the imaging paths, including AO performance vs. limiting magnitude.

Items.Authors: Michael Jones, Christopher B. Mendillo
Items.Title: Focal plane wavefront correction for dark hole creation with a neural network on PICTURE-D
Items.Abstract: In order to directly image exoplanets, a dark hole is created in the coronagraph science camera image, which is a region where light speckles are minimized to improve the contrast ratio. Creation of a dark hole normally consists of two independent steps: sensing and correction. During sensing, the electric field (EF) in the focal plane is determined, then during correction, a command is applied to the deformable mirror(s) to minimize the EF. The PICTURE-D balloon mission makes use of the linear EF Conjugation (EFC) algorithm for EF correction. However, this algorithm has two limitations: first, the corrections require a nonlinear model, whereas EFC relies on an inverted matrix, and second, EFC may not properly describe the optical system. Therefore, a neural network (NN) is developed for EF correction on PICTURE-D and will target the issue of nonlinearity. It is shown, in simulation, that a NN can obtain a higher contrast ratio after one iteration when compared with EFC.

Items.Authors: Hans J. Kärcher, Harald E. Nicklas
Items.Title: Four decades of technical progress in building Large Optical Telescopes
Items.Abstract: With the commissioning of the three Extremely Large Telescopes — GMT, TMT, and ELT — on the horizon, the era of the Very Large Telescopes is drawing to a close. Forty years ago, the progress in sensor technology and digital control culminated that astronomers’ dreams of building telescopes beyond the 4-Meter-Class became true. Active optics allowed the construction of large monolithic and segmented mirrors and initiated the worldwide planning and realization of very large telescope projects. The paper presents a comparison of the different design approaches of that time: an overview on their optical arrangements, the available mirror technologies and mechanical mounting concepts, including structural layout, axis mechanisms and related performance control strategies. The paper aims for an assessment of the technical progress from an engineer’s point of view that has been achieved over four decades, staying now at the transition phase to the new telescope generation of ELTs.

Items.Authors: Rubén A. Flores-Meza, Gerardo A. Lara, José Garcés, Carlos Espejo, Carolina Keiman, Beatriz Sánchez
Items.Title: FRIDA Instrument Testing, Evaluation, and Development Control Software (FITEDCS): Architecture, features, and achievements.
Items.Abstract: FRIDA (inFRared Imager and Dissector for Adaptive Optics of GTC) is a near-infrared imager and integral field spectrograph covering the wavelength range from 0.9 to 2.5 microns. FRIDA is working now in two observing modes: direct imaging and integral field spectroscopy.  FITEDCS is a system that allows an operator to command FRIDA mechanisms to select one of two modes of operation and several instrument configurations for acquiring images in FRIDA´s Detector. FITEDCS enabled us to successfully develop definitive control routines for all FRIDA mechanisms. The importance of such a system is great because of its essential contribution to the excellent performance of the FRIDA Instrument during several cryo-opto-mechatronic tests.

Items.Authors: Marco Colussi, Leo Colussi, Marco Mattietto, Gianmarco Franceschini, Andrea Fadalti, Nicola Casoni, Pascal Martinez, Mark Wallace
Items.Title: From final design to first alignment: advancements in the ELT Main Structure
Items.Abstract: The ELT Main Structure (MS), an alt-azimuth system weighing about 4500 t, is now undergoing advanced construction and early commissioning at Cerro Armazones. It mainly consists of a steel space-frame structure highly optimized to guarantee high dynamic stiffness, tight pointing performance, and controlled deformation. A dedicated 3D seismic isolation system ensures resistance under extreme site conditions. The paper outlines the final MS design and summarizes progress in manufacturing, erection, structural interfaces and initial alignment verification.

Items.Authors: Béatrice Lessard-Hamel, Rajbir Singh, Denis Brousseau, Frédéric Lamontagne, Hugues Auger, Simon Thibault
Items.Title: From manufacturing to optical performance: validation of the GIRMOS Image Slicer Assembly
Items.Abstract: Our team at the Advanced Optical Fabrication Infrastructure (AOFI) has been tasked with the fabrication of the slicer-based IFU for GIRMOS (Gemini InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph), which contains 42 270-μm wide slices along with the corresponding pupil and field mirrors. Here we present our manufacturing process, metrology, and assembly, including optical testing based on optical simulations. A complete metrology and assembly workflow was implemented using a ZYGO Verifire HD Fizeau interferometer, ZYGO Newview NX2 optical profiler, a coordinate-measuring machine (CMM), and a VIS/IR slicer test bench developed from the warm optical model. We have demonstrated that the slicer assembly meets the required optical performance at warm conditions and provides a robust basis for predicting its behavior in the final cryogenic environment.

Items.Authors: Jose Antonio Quero Reina, Elena Colomo, Guillermo Buendia
Items.Title: From Submission to Operations: A Proposal Handling System for Scientific Missions
Items.Abstract: From the opening of a Call for Proposals until the scientific proposals are finally ingested into a mission's operational environment, several months elapse. During this time, the proposal passes through various subsystems and phases: submission, approval, optimization, and finally ingestion. Integrating all of this presents significant challenges.    The goal for missions like XMM-Newton or XRISM, which handle numerous Guest Observer proposals, is to create a common framework, from the first PI’s initial request until the proposal has been approved and even observed. To achieve this, we are working on modern software that takes this traceability into account (XIPS for proposal submission, XPET for proposal evaluation), and we are developing new projects to close the entire cycle.    Additionally, we are developing new end-to-end environments in Kubernetes to validate complete integration across the entire Proposal Handling System.

Items.Authors: Xiang Ma
Items.Title: GECAM science operation
Items.Abstract: GECAM (Gravitational wave high-energy Electromagnetic Counterpart All-sky Monitor) is a constellation to monitor all-sky X-ray and gamma-ray transients in the multi-messenger and multi-wavelength era, which is composed of four instruments (GECAM-A,B,C and D). The primary science of GECAM are various types of gamma-ray transients. All GECAM telescopes are designed with the capability of triggering bursts in real-time and distributing trigger alerts promptly with short message service of Beidou satellite navigation system. This makes GECAM the first astronomical satellite in China with the capability of transmitting data in roughly real-time. To improve the detection of gamma-ray transients beyond the limitations of in-flight trigger software, the GECAM team developed a ground search system( ETJASMIN ) with advanced algorithms and high-performance computing resources. Initiated by the GECAM, a collective burst alert platform for astronomical transient (AstroBurstHub) has been developed.

Items.Authors: Qianhan Zhou, Lanqiang Zhang, Nanfei Yan, Jianhui Zhang, Xin Liu, Yongxin Zeng, Jinsheng Yang, Xuejun Rao, Changhui Rao
Items.Title: Global wavefront reconstruction strategy for dual-WFS Multi-Conjugate Adaptive Optics System
Items.Abstract: Dual-wavefront-sensing in MCAO improves wide-field correction, but conventional reconstructors often cause instability. We propose a global reconstruction strategy from a control perspective, incorporating the dual-sensor layout for stable estimation of ground-layer and high-altitude aberrations. Evaluated on an MCAO testbed simulating turbulence and multi-guide-star fields, it outperformed conventional single-sensor and cascaded schemes. On-sky tests on the 1.8-meter Chinese Large Solar Telescope further validate its suitability and robustness for wide-field adaptive optics applications.

Items.Authors: Nerea Castro, Armando Bilbao, Alberto Fernandez, Paula Sierra, Ángel Gomez, Lourdes Cabezuelo, Esther Fernández, Juan Martinez, Francisco José Sanchez, Miguel Martin, Arantza De Echenique, Rodrigo Pereira, Bruce Bigelow, Eduardo Villar, Christopher Madden, Miroslav Vulinovic, Francisco Meza, Hector Swett, Gustavo Arriagada
Items.Title: GMT site, enclosure, and facilities: facing the construction phase
Items.Abstract: In July 2024, the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT) enclosure design successfully passed its Final Design Review, achieving the “Ready for Construction” milestone and consolidating two years of detailed engineering. This phase prioritized a cost-effective and reliable solution, optimized for efficient construction at the remote Las Campanas site. The design integrates a wide range of disciplines—including structural (concrete and steel), mechanisms, MEP systems, telescope-specific utilities, control systems, telescope seismic isolation system and architectural elements—ensuring compliance with the observatory´s stringent technical and operational requirements.  Following this milestone, GMTO and IDOM have continued their collaboration to further enhance the enclosure´s performance, refine construction documentation and advance the development of additional summit facilities and infrastructure. Bi-parting shutter’s latching system, Summit Support Building are some of these examples.

Items.Authors: Marianne Cox, Sam Chan, Jose M. Filgueira, Efren Sandoval, Arushan Badasyan, Jorge Barrios, Rafael Ovando
Items.Title: GMTO cybersecurity strategies and integration with the GMT Observatory Control System
Items.Abstract: Large research institutions, such as observatories, face unique challenges in cybersecurity and are becoming more frequent targets of cyberattacks. It is critical that cybersecurity strategies are built into the design from the very beginning, and control measures are put in place to prevent vulnerabilities from arising as the observatory infrastructure evolves. GMTO is an active member and contributor of the Trusted CI Framework, a standard for cybersecurity programs tailored for research infrastructure, and have developed a Cybersecurity Program Strategic Plan (CPSP) to guide future updates. The Observatory Control System sits behind the cybersecurity-layer provided by the IT infrastructure, but requires secure access control for remote operations, interfaces with third-party services, and data life-cycle management. In this paper we describe the current GMTO cybersecurity implementation, and strategies for the integration with the Observatory Control System (OCS).

Items.Authors: Nicole Wolff, Bruce Macintosh, Saavidra Perera, Jayke S. Nguyen, Emiel Por, Jeffrey Chilcote
Items.Title: GPI 2.0 end-to-end simulations
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager Upgrade (GPI 2.0) is undergoing final testing before it is integrated into the Gemini North Telescope on Mauna Kea. The upgrade includes a pyramid wavefront sensor and advanced apodized-pupil Lyot coronagraph masks designed to block both telescope structures and bad DM actuators. In preparation for instrument commissioning and first light science, we present results of end-to-end simulations of the GPI 2.0 adaptive optics (AO) system and coronagraph that span AO control parameters, stellar magnitude, exposure time, and seeing. As part of this, we investigate the alignment tolerance of coronagraphic optics under atmospheric conditions realistic to Mauna Kea, as well as in the presence of non-common path errors. The result of these simulations is an exposure time calculator, which we demonstrate as a publicly-accessible GUI. Finally, we present simulations of Io, an extended object which will be observed during commissioning to validate AO performance.

Items.Authors: Saavidra Perera, Vincent Chambouleyron, Jérôme Maire, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Jayke S. Nguyen, Quinn M. Konopacky, Jeffrey Chilcote, Brian Sands, Randall Hamper, Matthew Engstrom, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Dan Kerley, Bruce Macintosh, Christian Marois, Fredrik Rantakyrö, Dmitry Savransky, Jean-Pierre Véran, Guido Agapito, S. Mark Ammons, Marco Bonaglia, Marc-André Boucher, Joel Burke, Ed Chapin, Daren Dilon, Jennifer Dunn, Simone Esposito, Guillaume Filion, Öykü Galvan, Jean Thomas Landry, Olivier Lardière, Duan Li, Alex Madurowicz, Teo Mocnik, Dillon Peng, Lisa Poyneer, Carlos Quiroz, Garima Singh, Eckhart Spalding, Nicole Wolff
Items.Title: GPI 2.0: calibration of the pyramid wavefront sensor
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager (GPI) is a high-contrast imaging instrument designed to directly detect and characterise young, Jupiter-mass exoplanets. After six years of operation at Gemini South in Chile, the instrument is being upgraded and moved to Gemini North in Hawaii as GPI 2.0. Several improvements have been made to the adaptive optics system as part of this upgrade. This includes replacing the current Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor with a pyramid wavefront sensor (PWFS) with a custom EMCCD, and employing the Herzberg Extensible Adaptive Real-Time Toolkit (HEART). These changes will increase GPI’s sky coverage by accessing fainter targets, improving corrections on fainter stars, and enabling faster and ultra-low-latency operations on brighter targets. The PWFS subsystem was independently built and tested to verify its performance before being integrated into the GPI 2.0 instrument. In this paper, we will present GPI 2.0 AO pre-shipping performance and calibration test results.

Items.Authors: Miska Le Louarn, Pierre-Yves Madec
Items.Title: Ground layer adaptive optics for 8-12m telescopes
Items.Abstract: In this contribution, we will outline the simulations made for a 12m wide field telescope, using ground layer adaptive optics (GLAO), on a 3-6' corrected field, in the visible.   We will present performance estimates using different methods, for a GLAO system using 3 natural guide stars.   First, simply filtering different amounts of layers in the Cn2 profile. Then, we will use a Fourier tool to present statistical information on the image quality improvements grought by GLAO. Finally, we will use a few End to End simulations to validate our findings.  We will show the distribution of image quality over a large number of measured Cn2 profiles, obtained by using a SCIDAR.  We also propose other concepts, like Rayleigh laser guide stars, and discuss the pros and cons of NGS and LGS in this context.

Items.Authors: Kuo-Chia (Alice) Liu, Lee Feinberg, Jeffrey Smith, Marie Levine, Charley Noecker, Joshua Abel, James Govern, Jon Lawrence, Jordan Effron, Gregory Walsh, Cory Smiley, Kenneth Dziak, Carson McDonald, Joseph Howard
Items.Title: Habitable Worlds Observatory: exploratory analytic cases formulation and analysis
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) is a NASA flagship space telescope designed to identify and characterize habitable zone exoplanets and advance our understanding of the universe through general astrophysics observations. Currently in pre-formulation, the project has defined Exploratory Analytic Cases (EACs) to address demanding science objectives while exploring challenging engineering parameters through architecture and trade space studies.    This paper describes the first three EACs and their lessons learned, discusses the integrated modeling pipeline, and shares key trade study results. These findings have guided EACs 4 and 5, which will further explore the trade space and prepare for the baseline design supporting the Mission Concept Review.

Items.Authors: Kieran McCall, Edgar Castillo Domínguez, Liam Boland, Matthias Tecza, Miriam Estefania Cisneros González, Eduard Muslimov, Eleni Sarakinou, James Kariuki, Sophie Paszynska, Angela Mills, Niranjan Thatte
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT - evaluation of opto-mechanical bonding: adhesive performance, substrate compatibility, and transportation viability
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics-assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. This paper presents an evaluation of Opto-mechanical bonding for the ISP by investigating various adhesives and substrates. It assesses their viability, performance, and manufacturability. The bonding is crucial in four main interfaces of glass to metal in the ISP:   1.Bulky, long and static collimator mirrors  2.Bulky and heavy static lenses in the infrared camera  3.Flat composite movable gratings in the Infared Grating Module (IGM)   4.Flat light movable mirrors for the Folding Mirror Mechanism (FMM)     All the information will be used in the updated design of the ISP.

Items.Authors: Jean-Emmanuel Migniau, Alexandre Jeanneau, Matthieu Guibert, Magali Loupias, Loïs Duran, Alban Remillieux, Victor Mauger-Vauglin, Eric Daguisé, Rémi Giroud, Nicolas Bouché, Pascal Huguet-Chantome
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT mount concept of mirror glued on Invar support
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. The Integral Field Unit (IFU) sub-system is part of an Integral Field Spectrograph cooled down to 130K. The IFU is in charge of splitting, slicing and rearranging the rectangular field of view into 4 long slits (~540mm) to feed 4 spectrographs. For encumbrance reasons, some mirror have been glued onto their invar support. This paper presents the design of one glued mirror case, the simulation of its thermal behaviour and the result obtained during testing a prototype inside a test cryostat. The conclusion summarises the foreseen results for the full IFU.

Items.Authors: Guillermo Mercant Rubio, Iago Funes Vecino, Alonso Álvarez Urueña, Laura García Moreno, Gonzalo José Carracedo Carballal, Irene Ferro Rodríguez, Heribert Argelaguet Vilaseca, Chiara Cerruti, Javier Piqueras López
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: design & tests on the current status of low order wavefront subsystem pick off arm engineering model (LPOA-EM)
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first-light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. Following a 2025 rescope phase, the project is resuming its final design. This review significantly impacted the Low Order Wavefront Subsystem (LOWFS) and its LPOU/LPOA unit, requiring the simultaneous operation of three LPOAs. This work details the opto-mechanical layout, electronic implementation, and planned tests for the LPOA Engineering Model (EM), adapted for HARMONI operation under MORFEO.

Items.Authors: Gonzalo José Carracedo Carballal, Irene M. Ferro Rodríguez, Iago Funes Vecino, Guillermo Mercant Rubio, Heribert Argelaguet Vilaseca, Alonso Álvarez Urueña, Laura García Moreno, Javier Piqueras López, Chiara Cerruti
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: LPOU calibrations for a micron-level pointing accuracy
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800 nm to 2450 nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25 mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025.    In previous designs, the geometrical calibration reference for the guiding probes took the form of a deployable calibration mask that could be inserted in the telescope's focal plane. In this work we explore the possibility of inserting the calibration mask closer the guiding probes, effectively decoupling optical and mechanical effects during the calibration process. The results of these analyses were performed and validated by means of optical simulations in RayZaler, and will be used to put bounds to the expected calibration accuracy achievable by this design.

Items.Authors: Miriam E. Cisneros-González, James Kariuki, Liam Boland, Edgar Castillo-Domínguez, Kieran McCall, Sophie Paszynska, Eduard R. Muslimov, Matthias Tecza
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: repeatability analysis of the spectrograph dispersers wheel mechanism
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-infrared integral field spectrograph for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The University of Oxford is in charge of the design and development of the four identical spectrographs that constitute the ISP subsystem. During the past few months, the spectrographs design has been substantially optimized to reduce the number of mechanisms exposed to cryogenic conditions. The updated version of the dispersers wheel module is a reduced size of the original Infrared Grating Wheel (IGW) presented in previous works. This work presents the different repeatability tests performed in the prototype mechanism, and the achieved stability results, including operation at room conditions, warm temperature in vacuum conditions, and cryogenic conditions.

Items.Authors: A. J. Eldorado Riggs, Garreth Ruane, Jorge Llop-Sayson, John J. Gill, Sofia Rahiminejad, Daniel W. Wilson, Camilo Prada, Emory L. Jenkins, Ramya Anche, Corey Fucetola, Ewan S. Douglas
Items.Title: High contrast testbed results with black silicon shaped pupils
Items.Abstract: NASA plans to image terrestrial exoplanets with the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). HWO's large primary mirror will most likely be segmented, which introduces extra diffraction in the image. Apodization, either with deformable mirrors or a dedicated mask, is needed to suppress this diffraction. Reflective apodizers for the Roman Coronagraph were flight qualified and demonstrated 4e-9 contrast in vacuum testbeds. In our current work, we aim to show that black silicon apodizers can provide the 1e-10 contrast needed by HWO. Last year for our first milestone, we showed that the incoherent light contribution from scattering off black silicon is negligible for the HWO contrast budget. Our next milestone is to achieve <5e-10 raw contrast on the Decadal Survey Testbed 2 bench in vacuum with a shaped pupil coronagraph. Here we present our most recent testbed results.

Items.Authors: Dijana Bogunović, Bernard Delabre, Tony Reed, Graeme Jonas, Andrew P. Rakich, George Maddever, Gergely Hajdu, Rolf Chini, Mikolaj Kaluszynski, Marek Gorski, Mirek Kicia, Grzegorz Pietrzynski
Items.Title: High resolution spectrograph for Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center (CAMK)
Items.Abstract: KiwiStar Optics/EOS Optical Technologies is contracted to build a high-resolution, low radial velocity (RV) spectrograph for Nicolaus Copernicus Astronomical Center’s (CAMK) Rolf Chini Cerro Murphy Observatory (OCM) at Cerro Murphy, next to the ESO-ELT in the Chilean Atacama Desert. The instrument is scheduled to be installed at the end of 2027, fiber-fed from the Nasmyth port of the F/7 Ritchey-Chrétien 2.5 m telescope currently being built by Astro Systeme Austria (ASA).  KiwiStar’s highly versatile KiwiSpec echelle R4-100, bench mounted spectrograph design, successfully implemented in MAROON-X and MINERVA North/South spectrographs, is upgraded to improve the stability and throughput of the system while keeping the same small footprint of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Clarissa R. Do Ó, Kane Sjoberg, Luke Lamitina, Susan Redmond, Dimitri Mawet
Items.Title: High-contrast spectroscopy testbed (HCST): low-order wavefront control loop in reflection of the vector vortex coronagraph (VVC)
Items.Abstract: The Astro2020 Decadal Survey has identified exoplanet imaging technologies as a top priority, especially for the design of the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), which must image and characterize Earth-like planets. Achieving this goal requires reaching and maintaining an extreme contrast of 1×10-10. The High Contrast Spectroscopy Testbed (HCST) in the Caltech Exoplanet Technology Laboratory (ETLab) is an in-air coronagraphic imaging demonstration testbed. Using a high-order deformable mirror and a vector vortex coronagraph (VVC), HCST has reached 1×10⁻⁸ contrast in broadband light. A low-order wavefront sensor (LOWFS) placed at the VVC reflection now tracks tip/tilt drift. We present results from implementing a tip/tilt control loop at the VVC reflection for the first time. Our results achieve an over 100x suppression of drift frequencies < 1 Hz.

Items.Authors: Andrea Orlati, Juri Roda, Gianpaolo Zacchiroli, Franco Fiocchi, Emanuele Santandrea, Carlo Migoni
Items.Title: High-frequency upgrade of the Gavril Grueff radio telescope at Medicina: results and performance comparison
Items.Abstract: The Gavril Grueff Radio Telescope underwent a major high-frequency upgrade featuring a new high-efficiency sub-reflector and an active surface system on the primary reflector.  This active system employs custom electromechanical linear actuators to dynamically correct gravity-induced surface errors.  This paper details the design of the actuators, primary panels, secondary mirror, and control software. High-precision photogrammetry verified the system's performance, confirming its ability to correct deformations and meet the surface accuracy targets required for high-frequency bands.  Finally, post-upgrade astronomical observations are presented. The analysis of these performance metrics confirms a significant enhancement in research capabilities and extends the telescope's operational potential at high frequencies.

Items.Authors: Ben Sappey, Ashely Baker, Jerome Maire, Andrea Lin, Quinn Konopacky, Nemanja Jovanovic, Samuel Halverson, Jean-Baptiste Ruffio, Bryson Cale, Rose Gibson, Stephanie Leifer, Jocelyn Ferrara, Rob Bertz
Items.Title: HISPEC Calibration Unit update: integration, testing, and performance
Items.Abstract: We present an update on the HISPEC Calibration Unit (CAL), a next-generation multi-source system enabling precision radial velocities, Doppler imaging, and high-contrast high-resolution spectroscopy of nearby exoplanets. Building on approaches from KPF, PARVI, and KPIC, CAL uses five NIR wavelength-encoded sources delivered via single-mode fibers for use during science observations or daytime calibrations. We have completed construction and begun integration and testing. Using PARVI, we show that all calibration modes provide the signal-to-noise needed for R=100,000 SMF spectroscopy. We assess stability of the y/J and H/K astro-etalons, and achieve absolute wavelength calibration from 0.98–2.46 µm using uranium hollow-cathode lines and gas cells. We examine all NIR sources for high-frequency fringing and use early HISPEC DRP versions to perform full Stage 0–2 calibration of PARVI, demonstrating its flexibility for SMF spectrographs.

Items.Authors: Olga Zamora, José Acosta, José Peñate, Teodora Viera, Marta Aguiar, Rosa Clavero, Joan Caseras
Items.Title: IAC80Pol: polarimetry with small diameter telescopes
Items.Abstract: IAC80Pol is a new dual-beam polarimetric capability proposed for the IAC80 telescope to enable high-cadence photopolarimetric follow-up of bright and moderately faint variable sources. Motivated by the growing demand for rapid characterization of transient events, the instrument combines a calcite analyzer and a rotating half-wave plate to measure linear polarization with low instrumental contamination. Simulations show that polarization uncertainties below 0.3% are achievable for sources around R≈17 with short exposure times. The design leverages previous successful implementations on similar small-aperture telescopes and aims to support studies of blazars, supernovae, GRBs, and other transient phenomena. Future extensions may include polarization mapping of extended sources and interstellar dust.

Items.Authors: Davide Mollica, Antonino D'Aì, Ciro Bigongiari, Fabio Pintore
Items.Title: iactsim: a GPU-accelerated IACT simulation framework
Items.Abstract: Performance evaluation and data analysis of next-generation Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) depend on large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. Although extensive air shower simulation is the main bottleneck, telescope response simulation can become quite time-consuming during the design and commissioning phases. To address this, we been developing iactsim, a GPU-accelerated Python simulation framework for IACTs. In this work, we demonstrate the framework capabilities simulating the telescope for the ASTRI mini-array project, ray-tracing the entire Schwarzschild-Couder optical system, and simulating the response of the ASTRI Silicon Photomultiplier Cherenkov camera. We present validation results comparing simulated data with data from the first two operational ASTRI Mini-Array telescopes and report preliminary benchmarks indicating a speedup of two orders of magnitude compared over the current CPU-based ASTRI simulator.

Items.Authors: Ilaria Ermolli, Roberto Cirami, Kamal Sant, Dario Del Moro, Paolo Romano, Bernard Gelly, Richard Douet, Giorgio Viavattene, Veronica Baldini, Fabrizio Giorgi, Mariarita Murabito, Luca Oggioni, Giovanna Jerse, Fabiana Ferrente, Lidia Contarino, Teodora Mihailescu, Antonio Sulich, Igor Coretti, Maurizio Oliviero, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Giorgio Calderone, Salvatore Luigi Guglielmino, Matteo Aliverti, Luca Giovannelli, Mauro Centrone, Etienne Pariat, Giorgio Frazzoni, Valentina Alberti, Roberto Piazzesi, Fernando Pedichini, Sara Bertocco, Edoardo Redaelli
Items.Title: IBIS 2.0: Interferometric BIdimensional Spectrometer 2.0 at the THEMIS Solar Telescope
Items.Abstract: The IBIS2.0 project aims to upgrade the Interferometric BIdimensional Spectrometer, originally operated at the Dunn Solar Telescope of the National Solar Observatory from 2003 to 2019, for its relocation and installation at the THEMIS solar telescope at the Teide Observatory. The refurbished instrument integrates the original dual Fabry-Perrot etalons with a new polarimetric unit, interference filters, new scientific cameras, and a fully modernised instrument control and data-handling system. These upgrades to the scientific sensors and the control system have enabled us to automate the instrument's operations. IBIS2.0 is designed to preserve the spectral coverage of the original system (580-860 nm) while offering enhanced stability and robustness.   The integration (Hardware and Software) of the instrument at THEMIS is currently underway. In this contribution, we present the installation progress at the new telescope as well as the new observational capabilities that it will offer.

Items.Authors: Michael P. Smith, Elliott Horch, Marsha Wolf, George Ayer, Matthew Buchkowski, Nicholas Devries, Sebastian Lucero, Kathleen Jurgella, Jacob Mader, Max Martone, Jessica McKeon, Fiona Powers Ozyurt
Items.Title: IFUSI: the Integral Field Unit Speckle Imager
Items.Abstract: We will present the progress of IFUSI, the Integral Field Unit Speckle Imager. This instrument, planned for the 4.3-m Lowell Discovery Telescope, will use a ~2100-fiber integral field unit to record spectra over a highly-magnified ~1.1 arcsec field of view. From these spectra, it will be possible to reconstruct speckle patterns which are then analyzed to produce diffraction-limited images. The instrument comprises a magnifier module, IFU, and four spectrographs. The magnifier module will provide a magnification of 60x to ensure that speckles are critically sampled. From the focal plane, the beam passes through two dichroic beamsplitters, which limit the wavelength range transmitted to the IFU. Additionally, the light reflected from the beamsplitters is also reimaged onto two EMCCD detectors, allowing for two “normal” speckle imaging channels. The IFU and fiber cable feed four modest-sized spectrographs designed to use COTS components, with the spectral images captured on four EMCCDs.

Items.Authors: Norihide Miyamura
Items.Title: Image-based wavefront correction in a sparse synthetic aperture telescope
Items.Abstract: Small satellites have been used for remote sensing with a spatial resolution of  several meters from low earth orbit (LEO) in recent years. However, it is difficult to  improve the temporal resolution for LEO remote sensing due to the short orbital  period. Therefore, the remote sensing technique which enables observation with  the high temporal resolution from geostationary orbit (GEO) or its nearby orbit is  getting important, especially in fields such as disaster monitoring. To improve not  only the temporal resolution but also the spatial resolution from GEO, an optical  system having a diameter of several meters is required because of the diffraction  limit of the optical system. we propose the Formation Flying Synthetic Aperture  Telescope (FFSAT). One of key issues is realizing the optical system with an  accuracy of less than 1/10 of the observation wavelength to get synthesized  images. Items.Authors: Yusufjon A. Tillayev, Azimjon Azimov
Items.Title: Impact of meteorological parameters to the observatory operation
Items.Abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of meteorological parameters measured at the Maidanak Astronomical  Observatory over the period 2012–2025, aimed at characterizing the site for the planned installation of a new 4 m  telescope. The study includes annual and monthly statistics of key variables such as wind speed and direction, air  temperature, and relative humidity, with more than 400,000 nighttime measurements analyzed for each parameter.  Long-term temperature trends are investigated, including a comparison with earlier (1996–2002) data to assess  potential signals of regional climate change. The results provide critical information on site stability and  atmospheric conditions, supporting both engineering specifications and long-term operational planning for future  astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Marcio Melendez, Laurent Pueyo, Nicolas Flagey, Randal Telfer, Matt Lallo, Jon Arenberg, Tiffany M. Glassman
Items.Title: Impact of micrometeoroids on HWO contrast stability
Items.Abstract: This paper presents ongoing investigations into the impact of micrometeoroid impacts on contrast stability for the coronagraph observations of the Habitable Worlds Observatory. We propagate properties of micrometeoroid impacts through precise coronagraph models that capture the spatial, diffractive properties of micrometeoroid-induced wavefront changes, as well as the temporal behavior of the spacecraft after impact. These calculations cover the case of micrometeoroid strikes on the telescope optics—primary or secondary. In the first case, the wavefront perturbation associated with the hypothetical impact will be localized on a primary segment or induce a secondary tilt, yielding a beam shear. In the second case, the observatory pointing will be perturbed.

Items.Authors: George Kosugi, Eisuke Morita, Hiroshi Yoshida, Kento Aida, Takeshi Nakazato, Kanako Sugimoto, Makoto Shizugami
Items.Title: Implementation and cost estimation of ALMA archive using cloud technology
Items.Abstract: The Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) currently archives nearly 300 TB of observational and processed data annually, totaling 2.3 PB. These data are first stored in Chile main archive and then copied to each regional archives in North America, Europe, and East Asia for permanent storage and provision to the science community. With the upcoming Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU), the data rate is expected to increase by an order of magnitude, raising concerns about escalating archive costs. Our group has evaluated commercial cloud platforms for hosting ALMA archives over several years. This presentation provides cost estimates for operating NAOJ's full archive on cloud services under current and WSU conditions, proposes a unified global architecture to ensure equitable access from each region, and assesses its operational costs. These findings provide a basis for strategic decisions regarding future ALMA archive operations.

Items.Authors: Chris Waring
Items.Title: Implementation of robust safety systems for the ESO VLT Telescope instrumentation with MOONS as case study
Items.Abstract: This paper provides instructional guidance on embedding safety compliance into ground-based astronomical instrumentation projects. It outlines a practical framework aligned with ISO 13849, the EU Machinery Directive, and ESO procedures, using the MOONS instrument as a case study. Topics include hazard analysis, justification and implementation of controls, and legal documentation. While rooted in ESO practices, the approach applies broadly to projects with EU partnerships. The paper includes procedural checklists and tools for validation, offering a model for safe and legally compliant design.

Items.Authors: Faouzi M. Boussaha
Items.Title: Implementation of SPIAKID (Spectro-Photometric Imaging for Astronomy with Kinetic Inductance Detectors) Instrument
Items.Abstract: We report on the implementation of SPIAKID (Spectro-Photometric Imaging for Astronomy with Kinetic Inductance Detectors) instrument. It will be dedicated to primarily observe and study ultra faint dwarf (UFD) galaxies in the Local Group. SPIAKID will use 130 x 130 pixel TiN-based MKID arrays that we will be arranged in a mosaic of 4 arrays to cover 2x2 arcmin field of view and operating in 400-1600 nm wavelength range, cooled down in a 100mK dilution cryostat. Here, we will give an overview of the instrument design by focusing on detector, optical system and readout electronics configurations that are being implemented.

Items.Authors: Thomas Mozdzen, Richard M. Scott, Philip D. Mauskopf, Isaac Smith, Mickey Martini, Mireia Perera-Gonzalez
Items.Title: Improved SNR by reducing timing jitter and using multiple bands in stellar intensity interferometry
Items.Abstract: We improve upon our intensity interferometry results from early 2024 of our observations of Sirius by using lower jitter firmware on our Swabian Timetagger and a shorter fiber optics cable with a graded instead of a step index. We also present preliminary results showing the suppression of t=0 crosstalk noise in the Timetagger by using two Timetaggers and a Synchronizer unit, which replaces the need for coax delay cable on a single channel that is susceptible to timing variations and thus jitter. Preliminary work using a spectrometer and a linear SPAD array to decrease data collection time while maintaining a strong SNR will also be presented.

Items.Authors: Saanika Choudhary, Dmitry Savransky
Items.Title: Improving the efficiency of dynamic completeness calculations for exoplanet direct imaging
Items.Abstract: Direct exoplanet imaging mission studies use dynamic completeness, the probability of detecting a planet given prior observations, to guide scheduling and estimate yield. Computing it is challenging: brute-force Monte Carlo is expensive, and common approximations often miss the true evolution of detectability. We analyze the numerical behavior of dynamic completeness, identifying cost- and accuracy-dominant steps, including repeated Kepler-equation solves and the mapping from orbital elements to observables. We further introduce a reduced-order uncertainty-propagation framework that carries orbital and photometric uncertainties through parameter distributions, enabling efficient, uncertainty-aware completeness estimates for the Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument.

Items.Authors: Chengkui Li, Shumei Jia, Juan Zhang, Yong Chen, Haisheng Zhao, Ju Guan, Xiaofan Zhao, Jingjing Xu
Items.Title: In flight energy calibration of EP-FXT
Items.Abstract: EP-FXT is a focusing soft X-ray telescope operating in the ~0.5–10 keV band, designed for sensitive follow-up imaging and spectroscopy of transient and variable sources. In orbit, we calibrate the energy–channel (EC) relation by fitting astrophysical emission lines and on-board calibration source. We construct and refine the response matrix files (RMFs). We also calibrate the grade distribution of events, quantifying the energy-dependent fractions of single- and multi-pixel grades. The calibration products ensure a stable spectral response, enabling reliable flux and spectral-parameter measurements for EP’s time-domain X-ray science.

Items.Authors: Eliad Peretz, john C. Mather, Stuart B. Shaklan, Ahmed M. Mohamed, Marc Boucher, Jean T. Landry, Christine E. Gregg
Items.Title: Inflatable starshade architectures for direct imaging of earthlike exoplanets
Items.Abstract: Inflatable starshades offer a path to achieving the large apertures required for direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets without the mass, volume, and deployment complexity of rigid architectures. We present an inflatable starshade design that integrates petal-based torus geometry, Kapton–resin laminates for post-deployment rigidization, and a simplified inflation system, enabling stowage within standard launch fairings. Recent structural and thermal analyses demonstrate that the inflatable framework can withstand lateral and vertical disturbances with acceptable safety margins, while identifying thermal gradients as the primary driver of dimensional instability. A baseline architecture is used to evaluate edge fidelity, deployment repeatability, mass drivers, and shielding strategies. We discuss requirements, risks, and the path toward sub-millimeter precision needed for 10⁻¹⁰ contrast. This work outlines the feasibility and remaining challenges of inflatable starshade

Items.Authors: Giulia Baroni, Riccardo Campana, Yuri Evangelista, Alejandro Guzmán, Paul Hedderman, Matthew Thomas, Michele Trenti, Robert Mearns, Miguel Ortiz Del Castillo, Ezequiel Marchesini, Giuseppe Dilillo, Giovanni Della Casa, Jack McRobbie, Airlie Chapman, Simone Pirrotta, Simonetta Puccetti, Matteo Perri, Andrea Santangelo, Wladimiro Leone, Sara Trevisan, Marco Citossi, Fabrizio Fiore, Tommaso Fagotto
Items.Title: In-flight performance and observations of the high-energy HERMES payload onboard SpIRIT
Items.Abstract: The Space Industry Responsive Intelligent Thermal (SpIRIT) mission is a 6U CubeSat developed through collaboration between Australia and Italy for high-energy astrophysics. The 6U CubeSat carries an actively cooled detector system in a Sun-Synchronous orbit. This payload is a compact X-ray and γ-ray instrument identical to the six units developed by INAF for the Italian Space Agency's HERMES Pathfinder mission. It is designed to detect and locate high-energy transients such as GRBs.  SpIRIT was successfully launched on December 1, 2023, aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9, and payload commissioning has been completed. Since June 2025, SpIRIT has been operating in standard Observation mode, with short daily activations and on-board data storage. This paper presents an overview of the orbital operations of SpIRIT's scientific payload, focusing on in-flight calibration activities and the analysis of scientific observations.

Items.Authors: Juan Zhang
Items.Title: In-flight performance of the background, timing and arf of EP/FXT
Items.Abstract: In this work, we present the in-flight performance of ​EP/FXT, including background characteristics, timing-system , and the effective area (ARF) of the two separate modules, ​FXTA​ and ​FXTB. The average rate of the in-orbit non-X-ray background for each module is ​∼0.04 counts/s/keV in the ​0.5–10 keV​ band. This rate shows good correlation with the event rate recorded in the ​pnCCD​ frame-store area, according which a background model is established. The FXT on-orbit timing system was calibrated using pulsars; the results indicate good consistency between ​FXTA​ and ​FXTB, and both are in alignment with ​NICER. After launch, contamination has degraded the ​ARF​ of ​FXT; this work details the decrease.

Items.Authors: Benjamin J. S. Pope
Items.Title: Information in interferometric and coronagraphic imaging
Items.Abstract: It is well-known that a diffraction-limited image contains only a finite amount of information about spatial structures in a scene. Using new analytic expressions for the interferometric visibilities of stars, and new calculations of Fisher Information matrices powered by automatic differentiation, we can quantify the degrees of freedom present in interferometric, direct, and coronagraphic images as a function of bandwidth, sampling, positioning, and field of view; and how prior information and complementary observations are best used to break degeneracies.

Items.Authors: Dominic F. Sanchez, Megan E. Eckart, Alex Geringer-Sameth, Benjamin Gerard, Waswa Waswa, Cesar Laguna, Alexx Perloff, Aditya Sengupta, Lisa Poyneer, Rebecca Jensen-Clem
Items.Title: Initial modeling and testbed feasibility studies of WaveDriver: a laser guide star AO system for HWO
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory will require >100× greater wavefront stability than achieved by JWST, pushing conventional telescope architectures to picometer-level performance limits. WaveDriver is a mission concept that relaxes these constraints by employing an external laser guide star (LGS) spacecraft flying in formation with HWO to enable wavefront sensing and control. Early results from the High Contrast Testbed demonstrate feasibility of required stability using coronagraphs, multiple deformable mirrors, and a suite of wavefront sensors. We report initial stability metrics, sensor performance comparisons, and an optical model quantifying anisoplanatic errors from finite LGS separation.     This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2013921.

Items.Authors: Neil T. Zimmerman, Tyler D. Groff, Guangjun Gao, Michael W. McElwain, Enrico Biancalani, Evan Bray, John Chambers, Roser Juanola-Parramon
Items.Title: Integral field spectroscopy with a Habitable Worlds Observatory coronagraph instrument: design concepts and technology demonstrations
Items.Abstract: In combination with a starlight suppression system, integral field spectroscopy is a promising technique for characterizing directly imaged exoplanets. In typical implementations, the region of interest around an occulted star is spatially sampled with a microlens array and spectrally dispersed in collimated space. The dispersed light is focused onto a detector to record a grid of spectra that can be remapped to a data cube. Here we describe reflective designs that improve the efficiency of the IFS cameras baselined by recent mission concept studies. By applying anamorphic magnification with freeform mirrors, the number of detector pixels per resolution element can be halved, significantly reducing the integration times needed to detect atmospheric absorption features. We also summarize plans to demonstrate the first combined operation of an IFS with a coronagraph in a vacuum testbed at contrast levels below 1E-9 over a 20% spectroscopic bandpass.

Items.Authors: Mo Zhang, Jingwei Hu, Yuan Liu, Chichuan Jin, Weimin Yuan
Items.Title: Integrating Grafana-Based visualization and collaborative toolchains to enhance scheduling and science operations in the Einstein Probe mission
Items.Abstract: This poster introduces an integrated engineering toolchain designed to support the EP mission’s scheduling and duty operations. A customized Grafana monitoring layer, built on top of mission databases and real-time data streams, provides engineering visibility into scheduling logic and observation-segment execution. These dashboards enable rapid visualization of the current observation timeline and serve as a useful aid for ToO submissions.    Complementing the monitoring stack, Feishu (Lark) is used as an operational control and notification platform, supporting automated duty alerts and coordinated communication. In addition, YouTrack provides an engineering-grade issue-tracking environment for managing anomaly reports, software defects, service-integration tasks, and long-term operational improvements.

Items.Authors: Helen M. McGregor, Max Hewlett, Nick Cerneaz, Sambath Non, Ross Zhelem, Dani Guzman, Qiongjie Lou, Jon Lawrence, Lew Waller, Jae-Woo Kim, Ho Seong Hwang
Items.Title: KSPEC: spectrograph optimization and delivery to the KMTNet telescope
Items.Abstract: The K-SPEC project is led by a consortium of Korean institutes, including Seoul National University (SNU), the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI), and the Korea Institute for Advanced Study (KIAS). The spectrograph will be installed on KMTNet and is a modified version of the TAIPAN spectrograph, which was previously installed and commissioned on the UKST at Siding Spring Observatory.     The KPEC spectrograph has been designed and developed by the AAO, building on the optomechanical expertise gained through the development of multiple spectrographs. This paper provides a detailed overview of the opto-mechanical build, emphasizing design choices that enable ease of manufacture, assembly, and alignment. Component fabrication, assembly, testing, and alignment were completed in early 2026, with first light expected by the end of 2026.

Items.Authors: Roxanne Ligi, Romain Petrov, Stéphane Lagarde, Sylvie Robbe-Dubois
Items.Title: Laboratory characterization of Hierarchical Fringe Tracking
Items.Abstract: One of the main limitations in long-baseline interferometry lies in its fringe tracking sensitivity. The challenge is therefore to maximize this sensitivity while minimizing the spreading of the signal on the detector. This is the goal at the core of the hierarchical fringe tracking (HFT) concept.  We present the laboratory characterization of the 2nd generation HFT chips operating in the near infrared (J and H bands) for up to 6 telescopes with more linear phase and group delay estimators, allowing a strong simplification of the tracking algorithm.   We show direct comparison of the limiting sensitivity of fringe sensing between 6-telescopes HFT and ABCD pairwise chips and demonstrate that the new HFT architecture provides a minimum (#telescopes-1) gain independently of the number of apertures.  Ultimately, this new chip is intended for implementation on the VLTI, CHARA or on the future Nanjing Purple Mountain Interferometer using three telescopes.

Items.Authors: Salah Oudjertli
Items.Title: Lanthanide-activated graphene for visible-IR interferometry and x-ray-correlated defect imaging
Items.Abstract: Advancing the integration of atomic-scale electronic engineering with high-precision optical diagnostics represents a critical frontier for materials science and intelligent manufacturing. Here, we introduce a lanthanide co-doping strategy in graphene—incorporating neodymium (0.5 at.%) and cerium (0.5–1.0 at.%) to activate optically responsive defect states that broaden graphene’s interaction with light from the visible to the near-infrared. Comprehensive structural and spectroscopic interrogation, combining Raman mapping, XPS, EXAFS, and time-resolved photoluminescence, reveals synergistic 4f–5d transitions that yield stable, wavelength-selective emission profiles spanning 400–1600 nm.  When integrated into wafer-scale architectures, the Nd/Ce co-doped graphene enables a >4-fold enhancement in hyperspectral contrast relative to pristine graphene, significantly boosting the sensitivity of visible–IR interferometric metrology. Items.Authors: Masashi Omiya, Hajime Inaba, Jun Nishikawa, Sho Okubo, Akira Arai, Yuki Moritani, Hideyuki Izumiura, Wako Aoki, Tomonori Usuda, Akito Tajitsu, Eiji Kambe, Bun'ei Sato, Toru Misawa
Items.Title: Laser frequency comb with an integrated fiber-feed system for Subaru/HDS
Items.Abstract: We report on an optical fiber-feed system for injecting an optical laser frequency comb into the High Dispersion Spectrograph (HDS) on the Subaru telescope. The comb, designed for HDS, provides evenly spaced emission lines with a mode spacing of ~30GHz across three wavelength ranges: 350-420 nm, 450-560 nm, 660-900 nm, using an erbium-doped fiber-based femtosecond laser. We developed the fiber-feed module (FFM) to deliver both stellar light and the comb beam to the HDS through the Nasmyth focus via optical fibers. The FFM consists of a fiber input system mounted on the AG/SH flange at the Nasmyth focus, a fiber and scrambling system, and a fiber output system that simultaneously feeds both optical paths to the HDS slit. This calibration system, integrating the comb and the FFM, enables highly precise measurements of stellar radial velocities and will contribute to research on exoplanets and distant galaxies.

Items.Authors: Reagen Leimbach, Shelley Wright, Jerome Maire, Aaron Brown, Bryson Cale, Man Yin Leo Lee, James Wiley, Maren Cosens, Chris Johnson, Renate Kupke, Evan Kress, James Larkin, Kenneth Magnone, Eric Wang
Items.Title: Liger at W.M. Keck Observatory: imager detector assembly and characterization
Items.Abstract: Liger is a next generation imager and integral field spectroscoper that utilizes a hybrid design to enable simultaneous observations with both setups. In this paper, we present the detector assembly, characterization, and readout processing results of the Liger imager. The focus position and distance of the assembly and the detector, pick-off mirror apparatus will be finely adjusted and tested in both warm and cold environments.
